elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity obligation to Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 appoints Vendor as “a non-exclusive provider,” and Section 12.3 expressly states that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment.

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to use Vendor as its sole supplier.
elements.evidence: The sole-provider language has been removed from Section 2.2. Section 12.3 also preserves Customer’s right to engage any supplier.

elements.element: Any exclusivity obligation applies only to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation exists under the rendered operative language, so there is no exclusivity extending beyond a defined product category.

elements.element: Any exclusivity obligation lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation exists under the rendered operative language, so there is no exclusivity lasting longer than 12 months.

elements.element: Any exclusivity obligation ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet applicable service levels.
elements.evidence: The condition for this requirement—an exclusivity obligation—is demonstrably absent because Section 2.2 is expressly non-exclusive and Section 12.3 disclaims any exclusivity commitment.

elements.element: Any exclusivity obligation ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet applicable delivery dates.
elements.evidence: The condition for this requirement—an exclusivity obligation—is demonstrably absent because Section 2.2 is expressly non-exclusive and Section 12.3 disclaims any exclusivity commitment.

result.reason: The operative amendment removes the sole-and-exclusive appointment and replaces it with an expressly non-exclusive appointment, consistent with Section 12.3. This fully achieves the preferred position through a narrow change, preserves Vendor’s appointment as a provider, and eliminates the prior contradiction between Sections 2.2 and 12.3.
